messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Error from runMI with MLR and modest N
parts:
Greetings,

I am running a second-degree polynomial trajectory model over 50 imputed datasets (N=226) using fun="sem" in runMI() (semTools v.0.5-3). I'm running into an error when I use MLR.

First, when I run the model on a single 50*N dataset with either ML or MLR, everything works as expected, so I don't think the model syntax (pasted at end) is the problem.

With ML:

stai <- runMI(fivepoint, data=distress.mi, fun="sem")

I get 11 warnings from runMI, none of which seems critical.

summary(stai) notes all 50 converged and a couple of Heywood cases, and, after appropriate-seeming model output, two warnings I can't parse. I'm including them here for any diagnostic value:

*******
Convergence information:
The model converged on 50 imputed data sets

Heywood cases detected for data set(s) 18, 30
These are not necessarily a cause for concern, unless a pooled estimate is also a Heywood case.

<model output, no Heywood>

Warning messages:
1: In if (attr(x, "information") == "observed") { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
2: In cbind(c1, c2, deparse.level = 0) :
  number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 1)
******

When I change to MLR
stai <- runMI(fivepoint, data=distress.mi, fun="sem", estimator="MLR")

I get the same 11 warnings, but summary(stai) returns an error, one of the same warnings, and no results:

******
The model converged on 50 imputed data sets

Heywood cases detected for data set(s) 18, 30
These are not necessarily a cause for concern, unless a pooled estimate is also a Heywood case.

Rubin's (1987) rules were used to pool point and SE estimates across 50 imputed data sets, and to calculate degrees of freedom for each parameter's t test and CI.

Parameter Estimates:

Error in if (attr(x, "se") == "robust.huber.white" && attr(x, "information.meat") !=  :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning message:
In if (attr(x, "information") == "observed") { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
*****************

I'd appreciate any help.

Pat

fivepoint <- '
m3 ~ BISQ_sleep_Arrangement_2opt_3m_c + Day_breastfeeding_3m_c
m6 ~ BISQ_sleep_Arrangement_2opt_6m_c + Day_breastfeeding_6m_c
m12 ~ BISQ_sleep_Arrangement_2opt_12m_c + Day_breastfeeding_12m_c
m18 ~ BISQ_sleep_Arrangement_2opt_18m_c + Day_breastfeeding_18m_c

i =~ 1*m0 + 1*m3 + 1*m6 + 1*m12 + 1*m18
s =~ -.833*m0 + -.5*m3 + -.25*m6 + .25*m12 + .75*m18
q =~ .6944*m0 + .25*m3 + .0625*m6 + .0625*m12 + .5625*m18

m0 + m3 + m6 + m12 + m18 ~ 0*1
i + s + q ~ 1
i + s + q ~ Infant_gender_c + F_PR_education_c + F_PR_age_c_s + M_PR_education_c + M_PR_age_c_s
i ~~ s + q
s ~~ q
'
--

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error from runMI with MLR and modest N
parts:
Hi Pat,

I have seen this problem a couple times before (defaulting back to the lavaanList method, from which lavaan.mi inherits), and have not yet been able to reproduce it or discover a reason for it.  Try re-installing semTools in a fresh R session, then restarting R before running your model again.  Try only loading semTools and running that part, so no other packages are loaded (other than the base, as well as lavaan automatically and all its dependencies).  Also, see if this happens to you even with the help-page examples (again, start in a fresh R session), which might help narrow down what else in the environment is interfering with R finding the semTools path to lavaan.mi methods.  

If it still occurs, please post your sessionInfo() output.  I might need output to see if I can reproduce it on my machine, so if you can find a brief enough example that generates your error using data you can share, that could help me track down the problem.

As far as obtaining your output in any case:  Even for the person for whom nothing solved the problem, she was able to access the lavaan.mi methods by explicitly calling them via getMethod().  

getMethod(summary, "lavaan.mi")(anx_bisqdur_lag)

Another option is to access the hidden functions behind those methods.  I've used the S3 method naming convention, so:

semTools:::summary.lavaan.mi(anx_bisqdur_lag)

Best,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
